Enum Class ADRCConfig.SystemOrder

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<ADRCConfig.SystemOrder>
yams.core.math.ADRCConfig.SystemOrder
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<ADRCConfig.SystemOrder>, Constable
Enclosing class:
ADRCConfig
public static enum ADRCConfig.SystemOrder extends Enum<ADRCConfig.SystemOrder>
Plant order for the active disturbance rejection controller.

The order is how many integrators sit between the motor voltage and the measured output: velocity loops on a DC motor are FIRST. For a position loop, POSITION and its aliases choose between first and second order when the controller is built, from the motor, gearing and inertia. The class documentation of ADRCConfig walks through choosing a value.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • FIRST

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder FIRST
      First-order plant: the loop commands and measures velocity, e.g. a flywheel or shooter wheel. The common case for FRC mechanisms.

    • FLYWHEEL

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder FLYWHEEL
      A flywheel's velocity loop; the same as FIRST.

    • SECOND

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder SECOND
      Second-order plant: the loop commands and measures position, and the mechanism's inertia sets how fast it moves. Position is the integral of velocity, so the plant is one order higher. POSITION chooses between this and a first order position loop for you.

    • THIRD

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder THIRD
      Third-order plant: the measured quantity sits two integrations behind the voltage. Rare; see the class documentation for when this applies.

    • FOURTH

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder FOURTH
      Fourth-order plant: three integrations between the voltage and the measurement. Rare; see the class documentation for when this applies.

    • POSITION

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder POSITION
      A position loop whose form is chosen when the controller is built from a motor config, from the motor's back-EMF time constant at the mechanism, J * R / (G^2 * Kt * Ke).

      When it is under ADRCConfig.SPEED_PER_VOLT_TIME_CONSTANT_PERIODS control periods, the motor's back-EMF, more than the mechanism's inertia, sets how fast it moves: each volt moves it at about the same speed, sooner than the loop can act. Its position is then a first order plant, with its speed per volt as b0. Otherwise its position is a second order plant, with its acceleration per volt as b0. Both are in the loop's units, rotations or meters for a linear closed loop. A heavily geared arm or pivot is usually first order, a lightly geared one second order.

      The time constant needs the mechanism's moment of inertia, set with withMomentOfInertia(...); without it, building the controller throws.

    • ARM

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder ARM
      An arm's position loop; the same as POSITION.

    • PIVOT

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder PIVOT
      A pivot's or turret's position loop; the same as POSITION.

    • ELEVATOR

      public static final ADRCConfig.SystemOrder ELEVATOR
      An elevator's position loop, in a linear closed loop; POSITION in meters. Without a moment of inertia, it is first order with its speed per volt as b0, since an elevator's speed is nearly always set by its motor's back-EMF. The motor config must use a linear closed loop.
